notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 30% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fourth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Yanni Gourde is on the injured non-roster list (hip surgery) and has not played this season.
Erik Černák is day to day and missed their last game. J.J. Moser has taken his spot beside Ryan McDonagh.
Max Crozier returned in their last game after missing 2 games.

story.head: The Jets need a win
paras: The Jets are winless in nine (0-7-2), and the Lightning (8-3-2) lost 5-4 in a shootout to Nashville on Oct 31. The Lightning won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-4 in Tampa Bay on Oct 29. The Lightning played last night, and the Jets are rested. Going in, the Lightning are fourth in the Atlantic (tied for eighth in the NHL) and the Jets seventh in the Central (tied for 27th).

The Lightning’s record (.692) is about what their chances are worth. The Jets have played better than their record (.367) says: their chances are worth about .433, and their finishing has held them back.

The Lightning (3rd) and the Jets (4th) both rarely ice the puck. The Lightning get into more chippy games than almost anyone (3rd) and let the point shots come and guard the net (4th). The Jets create more chances on the penalty kill than almost anyone (2nd), but take a lot of low-quality shots (30th). Winnipeg has scored 2.27 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. The Bolts are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Jets.

Nikita Kucherov (4 G / 14 A / 18 P in 13 GP) leads the Lightning in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Brandon Hagel (8 G / 8 A / 16 P in 13 GP) has a team-high eight goals. For the Jets, Kyle Connor (11 G / 4 A / 15 P in 15 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Mark Scheifele (2 G / 10 A / 12 P in 15 GP) is next in line.

Dennis Hildeby (2-0-1 / .885 SV% in 3 GS) will likely start for Tampa Bay, and Stuart Skinner (3-4-3 / .887 SV% in 10 GS) for Winnipeg. Skinner has a .840 save percentage in six starts against the Lightning, well under his usual .899. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
The Lightning usually control more of the chances than the Jets do.
